reasoning:
Cable 1 Kelvin pair (/SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO) remains unrouted: both nets carry open ratlines, kelvin_unrouted=1, gate_fail=1, gates_pass=false. Hard gate failure mandates repair.

Critical enforcement violation: Standing Rules 2 and 3 jointly require that ANY /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO net appearing in the previous round's failing_reasons MUST appear in the compiled stub nets list, and if absent, an explicit compile_failure must be injected and the FR dispatch aborted. This round's stub nets are ['/CAN_H', '/I2C_SCL', '/I2C_SDA'] — no Kelvin stubs at all. /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO were absent from stub nets, yet compile_failures is empty and FR was dispatched anyway. The pre-dispatch enforcement check either was not run or failed to fire its abort signal. This is a process gap: the rules exist but their gate mechanism did not hold.

The unconnected penalty (5.0/unit) is nearly invisible in the objective relative to DRC (50.0/unit) and kelvin/gate penalties (1000.0/unit). With unconnected=3 contributing only 15 points against a 34354 objective, FR has almost no score incentive to close the 3 open ratlines vs. optimising other metrics. Raising unconnected to 100.0 gives each open ratline 100 points of pressure — still below Kelvin/gate dominance, but enough to steer FR toward connection over cosmetic DRC cleanup.

The post-round enforcement audit is a new structural addition: it audits compliance with Rules 2/3 AS OF the round just completed (not only as a pre-check for the NEXT round), and propagates any gaps as mandatory compile_failure entries so they cannot be silently swallowed by an empty compile_failures field again. This closes the feedback loop that allowed this dispatch to proceed without Kelvin stubs.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Current weight 5.0 contributes only 15 points against a 34354 objective — effectively zero pressure on FR to close open ratlines. Two of the three unconnected ratlines are the failing Kelvin nets; penalising each at 100 points makes ratline closure a meaningful score lever without overriding the dominant kelvin_unrouted/gate_fail signals.

manager_rule: After each FR round completes and scores are recorded, perform a post-round enforcement audit: collect every /SENSEC*_HI and /SENSEC*_LO net from THAT round's failing_reasons, then check whether each appeared in the stub nets list that was used for THAT round's FR dispatch. If any Kelvin net was in failing_reasons but absent from the stub nets used — regardless of whether compile_failures was empty — record an explicit 'enforcement_violation' entry for that net in the round log (named by net, not just a boolean), and inject each such net as a mandatory compile_failure in the next round's pre-dispatch input before the set-membership check (Rule 3) runs. The post-round audit is the backstop when the pre-dispatch check fails to fire; it must run even if compile_failures is empty and the dispatch appeared to succeed.
